task.description: Validate lib/letflow/design/iss0343-backfill-missing-schema-tolerance.md against step-01's diagnosis and step-02's own acceptance criteria: typed error shape distinct from :tenant_not_provisioned added to Registry's affected specs; exact call sites (current_max query, insert, get_type query) identified with narrow Postgrex.Error postgres.code match (not blanket rescue); Backfill.run/1's new case clause treats the condition as skipped with no @spec/arity change; explicit rejection rationale for single-tenant scoping and fixture-lock-only alternatives; no implementation code (.ex code blocks) present.
acceptance_criteria: design doc maps step-01's diagnosed race to a concrete typed error shape (distinct from :tenant_not_provisioned) added to Registry's affected function specs
design doc identifies the exact call sites (current_max query, insert, get_type query) that must detect the missing-schema condition and how (Postgrex.Error postgres.code match, not a blanket rescue)
design doc specifies Backfill.run/1's new case clause treats the condition as skipped (not halted), with no change to its public @spec/arity
design doc explicitly states why scoping Backfill.run/1 to a single tenant_id, and why locking only the test fixture's DROP SCHEMA, are not chosen as the fix (or are noted as insufficient alone)
no implementation code (.ex code blocks) present -- signatures/specs/shapes in prose or @spec-style typespec blocks only

result.summary:
Four of the five acceptance criteria are satisfied and independently verified against the actual source: the design's :tenant_schema_missing error shape is correctly distinguished from :tenant_not_provisioned (Registration-row-exists-but-schema-gone vs. no-Registration-row); the three call sites named (insert_with_monotonicity_check/2's current_max Repo.one/2 query at registry.ex L229-233, its Repo.insert/2 at L247, and get_type/2's Repo.one/2 at L175) are exactly and only the three prefix:-scoped queries this module runs, confirmed by reading registry.ex in full, and the detection mechanism is correctly scoped to a %Postgrex.Error{postgres: %{code: :undefined_table}} match with explicit re-raise-on-anything-else language, not a blanket rescue; the design's quoted current @spec text for register_type/2 and get_type/2 (registry.ex L90-96, L164-168) and for Backfill.run/1 (backfill.ex L16-18) matches the real source verbatim, and the design correctly states Backfill.run/1's own @spec needs no change (confirmed: :tenant_schema_missing only adds one internal case clause, same skipped counter shape as the existing :tenant_not_provisioned clause at backfill.ex L36-41); and section 4 explicitly and substantively rejects both single-tenant scoping and fixture-lock-only alternatives with reasoning distinct from a rubber-stamp dismissal.

FAIL is on the fifth criterion, which is a single-check hard gate per WF-02 Step 1b rules (no partial credit): the design document contains real, directly copy-pasteable Elixir implementation code, not a signature/spec/shape. Section 2.3 (lines 134-141) presents a complete `case` clause -- `{:error, :tenant_schema_missing} -> Logger.warning("ISS-0332 backfill: tenant #{tenant_id}'s Registration row exists but its " <> "physical schema is gone (concurrent teardown/offboarding race), skipping") {:cont, {:ok, %{counts | skipped: counts.skipped + 1}}}` -- with a fully-formed Logger.warning/1 call, a real interpolated/concatenated log string, and a real map-update expression. This is not a @spec-style typespec or a prose description of control flow; it is a working function body ELIXIR-DEV could paste into backfill.ex verbatim, identical in kind to the existing real :tenant_not_provisioned clause it says it 'mirrors'. This is exactly the pattern the task's own instruction to CODE-DESIGNER ('Design only -- no implementation code') and this validator's own mandate ('no real .ex/.exs bodies -- signatures and type shapes only') forbid. By contrast, section 2.2's rescue_missing_schema/1 correctly stays at the @spec-only level (no try/rescue body shown) -- section 2.3 is the sole offending block, but one real .ex code block is sufficient to fail this gate outright.
result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER: rewrite lib/letflow/design/iss0343-backfill-missing-schema-tolerance.md section 2.3 to remove the literal case-clause code block (lines 134-141) and replace it with prose plus, if needed, a @spec-style shape only -- describe the new case pattern (match value, its Logger.warning/1 call's intent/content, and its skipped-counter outcome shape %{counts | skipped: counts.skipped + 1}) without writing the clause as executable Elixir. All four other sections passed verification against the real source (registry.ex, backfill.ex) and step-01's diagnosis and do not need rework.
